chapter: Duke, Eddie Lang and other guitarists
title: What Duke Ellington was really like
summary: Bunn found Duke a nice, alert businessman with common sense who kept people at a distance.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Was Duke -- Duke was kind of a hard man to know, wasn't he? I mean to really know him.
No.
I sort of have the impression -- I mean I've never met the man.
No, he wasn't. He was a very nice person.
You felt that he was for real.
Yeah.
I sort of had --
If anybody should know, I know.
Uh-huh. Some people have --
In other words, if he gave anybody else a bad time, I didn't get it.
Yeah, right.
And I wouldn't hear it. You know?
Uh-huh.
So whatever he done he took by himself -- to himself and done it, with his band.
Yeah.
Whatever hell he raised. But I didn't hear it. That's why I can't say nothing against him.
Some people have had the attitude that he was the kind of guy that he was everybody's friend but nobody could really get that close to him.
That's right.
You know, he kept people away a little bit.
That's right.
alert.
Yeah.
Duke'd always tell you [unintelligible] stayed (Unintelligible).
Alert. You mean on top of situations.
That's right. He was alert. He understood everything people were saying. Common sense, in other words.
Uh-huh. Do you think that's what made him such a good bandleader?
That's right.
Because there's a lot of people that are good writers that aren't necessarily good leaders.
Yeah. When he was stuck on himself he wasn't.
Yeah. He just wanted to get the job done.
That's right. Get it over with and get my money, that's all what I wanted. But he was a businessman.
